reachable: Yes, and the mechanism is exercised on the real path. `_train` calls `tmod.make_target(tgt, prev)` on the cmd-masked rows and the result IS the loss target, so the map is in the gradient path for all 4000 steps (steps defaults to 4000; TWM_STEPS is a wiring-test-only override). The module carries NO trainable parameters — buffers only — which matches its own DESCRIPTION and hypothesis; nothing needs gradient into it. Its state estimation is reachable: I confirmed on the real collate that prev_full's per-sequence zero row survives cmd_mask (exactly 64 all-zero z_prev rows for a bs=64 batch, one per batch element), so the segment detection works as described and is not a dead branch; the duplicate hash finds real structure (a 649-count class out of 1892 rows, plus classes of 41/22/20/15/13); 54% of training rows have an exact in-sequence duplicate. Freeze works: n_updates stops at exactly 600 and gains stop changing (0.7240/1.0347 at step 600 == step 800), and eval-mode make_target does not accumulate. Inversion is exact on the real path (round-trip relative error 8e-8, orthonormality error 1e-6), and the adapter's deepcopy-to-CPU of net.target_module keeps the frozen gains, so the map the model was trained under is the map the eval inverts. `max_rows=1024` truncates ~1892 rows to the first 1024, but r6 randperms the batch so the truncation is unbiased. End-to-end `H._train` with this genome runs clean on CPU. The honest limit on reachability: the effect SIZE is small (see divergence 2) — a ~2% amplification of the metric-relevant directions against a ~16% compression of the bulk, and a ~1% change in the loss value. This is far weaker than the description implies, but it is not inert.
solves_outside_model: No. Checked by reading every call site and by grep. (1) The module's only inputs are `z_obs` and `z_prev`, both plain observation embeddings — it never receives command text, path strings, the move list, window metadata, depth, or a step index; there is no string handling anywhere in the file and it imports only math/torch. (2) It never touches a model INPUT: `net(b["tok"], b["types"], b["key_pad"])` is called before make_target and `tok` is built by the stream's collate, which this module cannot reach. Its output is consumed only as the loss target. (3) At scoring time `to_obs` applies a single global rank-32 linear map (32 frozen scalars in a fixed basis) to the model's prediction, identically for every window; the candidate bank is left untouched, so the N-way argmin metric itself is unchanged. (4) Both arms of the differential get the SAME target_mod instance (cups_ca.measure_trained_net passes it to both CP.measure and CP.alt_chain, and cups_probe applies to_obs at all three sites), so the map is common-mode across native and role-swapped chains and cannot produce an asymmetry. (5) The map is estimated only from training-split observation statistics during the first 600 steps and frozen thereafter; there is no path from an eval window's routing to the 32 gains, and 32 global scalars could not encode per-window answers even if there were. This is the legitimate "shaping a LOSS" case, not the retracted "compute the routing in Python and hand it to the model" shape.
summary: The code is a faithful, well-behaved implementation of an exactly-invertible frozen linear target reparametrization, and it is clean on the shortcut question: nothing about the move chain reaches the model, the map is global and applied identically to both arms of the differential, and the eval metric is untouched. Every mechanical claim I could execute checks out — exact inversion (8e-8), orthonormality (1e-6), basis converged to the true top-32 eigenspace, trajectory detection from the all-zero z_prev (64 starts per 64-sequence batch), duplicate down-weighting finding a real 649-row empty-observation class, gains starting at exactly 1, ramping, and freezing at update 600, and exact preservation of the objective's equality classes. The hypothesis's factual premises about the data are also true: 640/640 cups windows have the withheld read observation exactly equal to one exposure candidate, and 54% of training rows have an exact in-sequence duplicate. What does NOT hold is the description of WHY the map is what it is, and how big it is. The hypothesis says gains come from the within-trajectory fraction of each direction's variance; the code divides by an UNCENTERED second moment, and on the real training root the squared weighted mean is 50% and 26% of that denominator on precisely the two directions that carry the entire map. Recomputing with the centered moment the hypothesis names would give those directions gains 1.009 and 0.983 and collapse the whole map to [0.983, 1.017] — a near-identity — with correlation 0.066 between the code's gains and the described mechanism's gains. So the realized map is "shrink the two directions with the largest duplicate-reweighted mean offset" (an empty-observation axis, which is a WITHIN-trajectory direction, the opposite of the claimed compression target), not "amplify within-trajectory contrast". The realized spectrum is [0.724, 0.861, then 30 gains in 0.988-1.035]: no amplification side worth the name, the 3x cap never binds, foil-relevant directions get 1.021x against 0.836x for the bulk, and the loss value moves ~1%. The author explicitly pre-declared this near-identity outcome as their benign failure case 1, which is to their credit, but the archive entry as written would tell a later reader the mechanism did something it did not do.

divergences.claim: "g_i = ... r_i = (v_i^T W v_i) / (v_i^T T v_i), the fraction of that direction's variance that occurs WITHIN a trajectory rather than between trajectories" and "directions that only separate one system/trajectory from another are compressed".
divergences.what_the_code_does: T is an UNCENTERED weighted second moment (`total = z.t() @ zw`, line 115), not a variance. The duplicate down-weighting the author added (weight 1/649 for the 649 identical empty-observation rows in a 1892-row batch) shifts the weighted population mean far off zero along the empty-vs-nonempty axis, and that mean^2 term then dominates T on exactly the directions that end up carrying the whole map. Measured on the real train root: the two directions that receive the only non-trivial gains (0.724 and 0.861) have mean^2/T = 0.504 and 0.260. Recomputing the identical pipeline with a centered total moment — the quantity the hypothesis names — gives those directions gains 1.009 and 0.983, and collapses the entire gain spectrum to [0.983, 1.017], i.e. essentially the identity map. Correlation between the code's 32 gains and the gains the stated definition would produce is 0.066 (0.086 on a second seed). So the map the model actually trains under is "shrink the two directions with the largest duplicate-reweighted mean offset", not "amplify within-trajectory directions and compress between-trajectory ones". The two compressed directions are in fact a WITHIN-trajectory axis (the empty mv/redirect observation vs everything else: duplicate rows project onto them with std exactly 0.000, mean +12.48 / -10.34, against non-dup mean -6.57 / +5.45).
divergences.evidence: Ran 600 warmup updates through the real collate + cmd_mask + prev-shift path on data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, accumulating a centered total moment in parallel. Table (i, code gain, gain-if-centered, r_uncentered, r_centered, mean^2, T, W): (1, 0.724, 1.009, 0.471, 0.951, 47.79, 94.76, 44.61); (0, 0.861, 0.983, 0.666, 0.902, 42.23, 162.40, 108.09); (2, 0.988, 1.011, 0.877, 0.954, 3.71, 47.09, 41.31). Reproduced at seed 1.

divergences.claim: "Net effect: directions along which observations differ inside one trajectory are amplified in target space, and directions that only separate one system/trajectory from another are compressed, by at most 3x either way"; synthetic reference "purely-between directions converged to gain 0.35, purely-within directions to 1.42".
divergences.what_the_code_does: On the real root the realized spectrum after the 600-update warmup is [0.724, 0.861, 0.988, then 29 gains in 1.003-1.035]. There is essentially no amplification side (max 3.5%); the +-log(3) cap never binds. Measured directional effect of the frozen map: the foil-pair difference directions that comp_ca's N-way pick actually reads are amplified 1.021x (median 1.021, p10 1.015, p90 1.027, over all 3148 within-window candidate pairs of the inner split); random cross-corpus obs-pair differences 0.836x; isotropic random directions 1.000x; raw obs rows 0.912x. So the reweighting toward the metric-relevant directions is real but ~22% in relative terms, and the objective's loss value moves ~1.2% (1.8195 identity vs 1.7978 equalized on a matched synthetic-error batch). This is the author's own pre-declared "benign failure case 1", which they were honest enough to name — but the hypothesis states the amplification as the net effect, and a reader of the archive would infer a stronger mechanism than the code delivers. Practical consequence for attribution: whatever this genome scores, the target axis contributes a mild reweighting and the objective swap (r12 -> r22) is the dominant change.
divergences.evidence: Frozen gains printed after 600 real updates; amplification measured as ||M v|| / ||v|| over the real foil banks from CP.load_cups_context(root,'inner') and over corpus samples.

divergences.claim: "with the log-mean of the gains held at zero so the overall loss scale and the loss's per-coordinate precision weighting are not moved".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The log-mean IS held at zero (measured -2.8e-9; the clamp never engages so the centering is exact), which fixes det(M)=1. But det-1 is not loss-scale invariance: the map shrinks actual target row norms by 8.8% and squared distances among real rows by ~17%, and the per-coordinate variance profile is materially rearranged (per-coordinate variance ratio min 0.640, max 1.033, mean 0.899; corr(v_old, v_new) = 0.489). Against the objective's fixed constants (_TEMP=0.25, _MARGIN=0.5) that is a small effective-temperature/margin change, not zero. Measured net loss change 1.2%, so the practical size is minor even though the claim as written is false.
divergences.evidence: tgt vs make_target(tgt) on a real batch; loss comparison through evolve.chunks.objective.r22_exact_target_equivalence_quotient.

divergences.claim: "Because that map is a bijection, it also preserves the objective's exact-equality classes exactly - identical rows stay identical (verified: transformed duplicate distance is exactly 0.0)".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Holds as measured: on a real batch the equivalence matrix under the objective's test is bit-for-bit unchanged (0 differing pairs) and the max deviation inside a transformed duplicate class is exactly 0.0. The claim's reasoning is nonetheless slightly wrong: r22's class test is a TOLERANCE (`tt_raw <= 1e-5`), not exact equality, and the map's smallest singular value 0.724 can shrink a squared distance by up to 1.9x, so a distinct pair sitting just above the tolerance could be pulled into a class. Not observed on this data; flagged as an unexercised edge rather than a defect.
divergences.evidence: Recomputed r22's `equivalent` matrix on tgt and on make_target(tgt) for a real 1892-row batch.

divergences.claim: "V is carried by orthogonal iteration on the total moment (re-orthonormalized every 4 updates by twice-repeated Gram-Schmidt)".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The power step and the re-orthonormalization happen TOGETHER every 4 updates (both sit after the `n_updates % refresh_every` early return), i.e. 150 iterations over the warmup rather than 600 power steps with periodic re-orth. Verified harmless: the final basis spans the true top-32 eigenspace of total_moment (principal-angle singular values all >= 0.9725, mean 0.9983) and its Rayleigh quotients match the top eigenvalues to two decimals (162.4, 94.76, 47.09, 40.45, ...).
